statement: In triangle $ABC$, point $D$ is the midpoint of $\overline{BC}$ and point $E$ is the midpoint of $\overline{CA}$. Segments $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{BE}$ meet at point $G$. The area of triangle $ABC$ is $54$. What is the area of quadrilateral $GDCE$?

choices.misconception: I knew the three medians cut the triangle into six equal pieces of area 9, but I counted the quadrilateral as only one piece.
I found triangle CDE, which is a quarter of the triangle, 13.5, and forgot the small triangle GDE that is also inside the quadrilateral.
I took triangle ADC, which is half of the triangle, as if the quadrilateral filled all of it.
I subtracted triangle ABG, which is a third of the triangle, from the whole, but that still leaves triangles AGE and BGD in my answer.

hints: Draw the third median, from $C$ through $G$ to the midpoint of $\overline{AB}$. The three medians cut the triangle into six small triangles.
The six small triangles all have the same area.
Each small triangle has area $54 / 6 = 9$, and quadrilateral $GDCE$ is made of two of them.

solutions.reliable: Median $\overline{BE}$ splits triangle $ABC$ into two triangles of equal area, so triangle $BCE$ has area $27$. The medians meet at the centroid $G$, which is two thirds of the way from $A$ to $D$, so $GD = \frac{1}{3}AD$. Triangles $BGD$ and $BAD$ share the height from $B$, so triangle $BGD$ has $\frac{1}{3}$ the area of triangle $BAD$, which is $\frac{1}{3} \cdot 27 = 9$. Quadrilateral $GDCE$ is triangle $BCE$ minus triangle $BGD$, so its area is $27 - 9 = 18$.
solutions.elegant: The three medians cut any triangle into six small triangles of equal area, here $54 / 6 = 9$ each. Quadrilateral $GDCE$ consists of the two small triangles $GDC$ and $GCE$, so its area is $18$.
